stem: When assessing poor growth in a child without a genetic condition, which measurement is typically spared?
explanation: Head circumference is typically spared in poor growth without an underlying genetic condition.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Head circumference is a useful discriminator in growth assessment because it is often preserved when weight and length are affected.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because head circumference is typically spared in poor growth without an underlying genetic condition.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because weight is commonly affected early in poor growth.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because length or height may also be affected.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because body mass index may be reduced in poor growth.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because mid-parental height is a target for growth assessment, not a child’s spared measurement.
